submitted.rationale: Index 3 (Co0.83Sb0.17) had the highest measured EQE, 0.0040%. It sits at the Co5SbO8 spinel composition, which MACE puts on the hull. EQE rose steadily toward the Co-rich end: idx19 about 0, idx6 0.0021%, idx3 0.0040%.

rejected.reason: Trirutile CoSb2O6 is on the MACE hull, but its measured EQE was about 0 (-0.0001%).
The Co7Sb2O12 spinel region gave 0.0021% EQE, about half of index 3.

consultations.verdict: Support: MACE puts trirutile CoSb2O6 on the hull (0 eV/atom), so it should form near Sb=0.667 (index 19). MEGNet's HSE gap of 0.37 eV is low, which argues weakly against, but MEGNet often underestimates gaps in Co d-block oxides, and absorption at 2.4 eV is fine either way. Measure 19 first as the anchor for the stable ternary phase.

Support: MACE puts spinel Co7Sb2O12 (Sb=0.222) only 0.03 eV/atom above the hull, so it is likely to form near index 6 (Sb 0.238). Its MEGNet HSE gap of about 1.4 eV (receipt 6d46b81d7bc9) means it absorbs at 2.4 eV. The trirutile end measured roughly 0 EQE, so moving to the Co-rich spinel region is the most informative next step.

Support: MACE puts spinel Co5SbO8 (Sb=0.167) on the hull (0.0002 eV/atom), so single-phase spinel should form at index 3 (Sb 0.167). EQE is higher on the Co-rich side (idx6 0.0021 vs idx19 about 0), and the GP also favours the Co-rich region. I'm spending the last measurement on this stable spinel composition.
